q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Supplementary Grant' from an 'Excess Grant'?

options.A: A Supplementary Grant is voted after the year ends, whereas an Excess Grant is voted during the year
options.B: Both are voted before any expenditure is incurred
options.C: A Supplementary Grant is obtained during the financial year when the amount already granted for a service proves insufficient, whereas an Excess Grant is obtained after the close of the year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the grant
options.D: A Supplementary Grant needs no vote of Parliament, whereas an Excess Grant is charged on the Consolidated Fund

e: A Supplementary Grant is obtained during the financial year when the amount already granted for a service proves insufficient. An Excess Grant is obtained after the close of the year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the grant, so option C is correct.

q: A 'token' provision is made in a Demand for Grants for a new work or service when:

options.A: The funds required for the work or service during the year are intended to be found by re-appropriation from savings within the grant, the token provision being made to obtain the approval of Parliament to the new item
options.B: The work is to be financed entirely from market borrowings
options.C: The expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: The work has already been completed in the previous year

e: A token provision is made in a Demand for Grants when the funds for a new work or service during the year will be found by re-appropriation from savings within the grant, the token provision serving to obtain Parliament's approval to the new item.

q: The apportionment of through-traffic earnings is carried out among the zonal railways every month. Its net effect on the total gross earnings of the Indian Railways taken as a whole is that the total:

options.A: Increases by the amount of terminal charges collected
options.B: Decreases by the amount held under Traffic Suspense
options.C: Is shared equally among all the zonal railways
options.D: Remains unchanged, apportionment merely distributing the same earnings among the railways over which the traffic has passed

e: Apportionment only distributes the same through-traffic earnings among the railways over which the traffic passed. It does not create or destroy earnings, so the total gross earnings of Indian Railways as a whole remain unchanged.

q: A through passenger ticket is issued for a journey which passes over two zonal railways of unequal length. In the apportionment of the coaching earnings from this ticket, the share of each railway is worked out broadly in proportion to:

options.A: The number of coaches owned by each railway
options.B: The distance over which the passenger is carried on each railway
options.C: The number of originating passengers booked on each railway
options.D: The capital-at-charge of each railway

e: Coaching earnings from a through passenger ticket are apportioned among the railways concerned broadly in proportion to the distance over which the passenger is carried on each railway, as in Part A of the Traffic Book.

q: The earnings from parcels and luggage booked by coaching trains on a zonal railway are taken to account, for the purpose of apportionment in the Traffic Book, under:

options.A: Part A of the Traffic Book, which deals with Coaching earnings
options.B: Part B of the Traffic Book, which deals with Goods earnings
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings, which are never apportioned
options.D: The Public Account of India

e: Parcels and luggage are coaching traffic, and their earnings are apportioned under Part A of the Traffic Book, which deals with Coaching earnings. Part B deals only with Goods earnings, so option A is correct.

q: In the allocation of an item of capital expenditure on a zonal railway, the elements of the allocation string, read in order, broadly indicate:

options.A: Only the name of the contractor to whom payment is to be made
options.B: The source of finance (fund), the Plan Head of the work and the Primary Unit (object) of expenditure
options.C: Only the month in which the expenditure was incurred
options.D: Only the division in which the work is situated

e: The allocation string for capital expenditure shows, in order, the source of finance or fund, the Plan Head of the work and the Primary Unit or object of expenditure, which together fix how the item is classified and financed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Pension Fund is credited by appropriation from revenue.
2. The pensionary charges of the Railways are met by debit to the Railway Pension Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Railway Pension Fund is credited by appropriation from revenue to build up the fund, and the pensionary charges of the Railways are met by debit to that fund, so both statements are correct.

q: The Capital Fund of the Railways is credited mainly with appropriations made out of:

options.A: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.B: The safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.C: The deposits of contractors held in the Public Account
options.D: The surplus of the Railways, after meeting dividend (while it was payable) and other charges, available for financing capital works from internal resources

e: The Capital Fund is credited mainly with appropriations out of the surplus of the Railways, after meeting dividend while it was payable and other charges, and that surplus finances capital works from internal resources, so option D is correct.

q: If the annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is kept persistently below the level warranted by the renewals falling due, the consequence in the railway accounts and working is that:

options.A: Arrears of renewals and replacements accumulate, affecting the condition and safety of assets, even though the working expenses of the year appear lower
options.B: The Operating Ratio of the year automatically becomes more favourable in a real sense
options.C: The balance in the Pension Fund increases correspondingly
options.D: The capital-at-charge of the Railways is reduced by the amount of under-provision

e: The DRF must be provided at the level warranted by renewals falling due. Persistent under-provision lets arrears of renewals and replacements accumulate and affects asset condition and safety, even if the year's working expenses look lower.

q: A zonal railway takes up the elimination of a level crossing by constructing a road over-bridge as a safety work and proposes to finance works of this class from the fund credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares and a share of the cess on diesel and petrol. That fund is the:

options.A: Capital Fund
options.B: Railway Safety Fund
options.C: Debt Service Fund
options.D: Development Fund

e: The fund credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares and a share of the cess on diesel and petrol, used for safety works such as elimination of level crossings, is the Railway Safety Fund, so option B is correct.

q: A zonal railway proposes the renewal and upgradation of signalling and track assets which have become due for replacement on safety considerations, and seeks finance from the dedicated safety corpus created in the Budget of 2017-18 for safety-related works of renewal, replacement and upgradation. The fund referred to is the:

options.A: Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Railway Safety Fund
options.C: Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.D: Capital Fund

e: The dedicated safety corpus created in the Budget of 2017-18 for safety-related works of renewal, replacement and upgradation is the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, distinct from the older Railway Safety Fund, so option C is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the General Books from the Subsidiary Books of a zonal railway?

options.A: The General Books record only stores transactions, whereas the Subsidiary Books record only cash transactions
options.B: Both sets of books are rendered monthly to the Railway Board
options.C: The General Books are maintained only in the workshops, whereas the Subsidiary Books are maintained only at stations
options.D: The Subsidiary Books record the transactions in detail in the first instance, whereas the General Books record the compiled and classified results posted from the subsidiary books and summaries

e: Subsidiary Books record transactions in detail in the first instance. The General Books record the compiled and classified results posted from the subsidiary books and summaries, so option D states the distinction correctly.

q: To accommodate the large number of year-end adjustments, the Account Current of a zonal railway for the month of March is rendered in two parts, which are known as the:

options.A: March (Preliminary) Account Current and the March (Final) Account Current
options.B: March Account Current and the April Account Current
options.C: Approximate Account Current and the Single Account Current
options.D: Revenue Account Current and the Capital Account Current

e: To accommodate the large number of year-end adjustments, the March Account Current is rendered in two parts: the March (Preliminary) Account Current and the March (Final) Account Current, so option A is correct.

q: Inter-railway transfer transactions of the zonal railways, after acceptance, are finally adjusted and cleared through the head 'Transfer Railways' maintained in the books of:

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Pay and Accounts Office of the Ministry of Finance
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Inter-railway transfer transactions, after acceptance by the respondent railway, are finally adjusted and cleared through the head Transfer Railways maintained in the books of the Railway Board, so option B is correct.

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' is operated to record:

options.A: The Provident Fund subscriptions recovered from the staff
options.B: The cheques issued by the railway but not yet encashed
options.C: The amounts remitted by the Cash Office and stations into the accredited bank, pending their adjustment against 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'
options.D: The transfer certificates issued to other railways

e: Remittances into Banks is operated to record amounts remitted by the Cash Office and stations into the accredited bank, pending their adjustment against Deposits with Reserve Bank, so option C is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Appropriation Act from the Appropriation Accounts?

options.A: The Appropriation Act is prepared by the C&AG, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are passed by Parliament
options.B: Both are prepared by the zonal railways at the close of the year
options.C: The Appropriation Act is an accounts document, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are a law
options.D: The Appropriation Act is the law passed by Parliament authorising withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund up to the amounts granted, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are the accounts prepared after the close of the year comparing the actual expenditure with the final grant

e: The Appropriation Act is the law passed by Parliament authorising withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund up to the amounts granted. The Appropriation Accounts are prepared after the year comparing actual expenditure with the final grant, so option D is correct.

q: The 'Final Grant' of a zonal railway for a financial year represents:

options.A: The original grant as voted by Parliament, together with supplementary grants obtained and as modified by re-appropriations sanctioned during the year
options.B: Only the Budget Estimates as originally presented to Parliament
options.C: Only the Revised Estimates as framed in September
options.D: The grant of the following year taken on account

e: The Final Grant is the original grant voted by Parliament, together with supplementary grants obtained during the year and as modified by re-appropriations sanctioned during the year, against which actuals are compared in the Appropriation Accounts.

q: The Operating Ratio of the Railways for a year broadly expresses:

options.A: The ratio of capital expenditure to revenue expenditure of the year
options.B: The ratio of the working expenses of the year to the gross earnings of the year, expressed as a percentage
options.C: The ratio of goods earnings to coaching earnings of the year
options.D: The ratio of the Pension Fund balance to the total pensionary charges

e: The Operating Ratio expresses the working expenses of the year as a percentage of the gross earnings of the year. A lower ratio indicates that a smaller share of earnings is consumed by working expenses, so option B is correct.

q: The Net Revenue of the Railways for a financial year is arrived at by deducting, from the gross earnings of the year:

options.A: Only the dividend payable to General Revenues
options.B: Only the capital expenditure incurred during the year
options.C: The total working expenses of the year, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund
options.D: The total balances held under the suspense heads at the close of the year

e: Net Revenue is gross earnings minus total working expenses, and total working expenses include the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund as well as ordinary working expenses, so option C is correct.

q: The balance under Stores Suspense, exhibited under Plan Head 71 in the capital classification, broadly represents:

options.A: The amounts recoverable from staff for stores lost in transit
options.B: The cheques issued for stores purchases but not yet encashed
options.C: The earnings of stores depots from the sale of scrap
options.D: The value of stores in stock with the Railways, purchased and held pending issue for works and maintenance

e: The balance under Stores Suspense, under Plan Head 71, represents the value of stores in stock with the Railways, purchased and held pending issue for works and maintenance, and not amounts recoverable or depot earnings.

q: A workshop accountant proposes to book the labour and material locked up on unfinished jobs under Plan Head 71, which covers Stores Suspense. The correct position is that such balances on jobs in progress belong to:

options.A: Manufacturing Suspense under Plan Head 72
options.B: Stores Suspense under Plan Head 71
options.C: Miscellaneous Advances under Plan Head 73
options.D: Other Specified Works under Plan Head 64

e: Labour and material locked up on unfinished workshop jobs is a balance of jobs in progress and belongs to Manufacturing Suspense under Plan Head 72. Plan Head 71 covers only stores in stock under Stores Suspense, so option A is correct.

q: The earnings collected at a station of a zonal railway pass, in their journey to final adjustment in the Government accounts, broadly through the sequence:

options.A: Station, Railway Board, Ministry of Finance
options.B: Station, Cash Office of the railway, accredited bank and the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank at Nagpur
options.C: Station, Pay and Accounts Office, Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: Station, Traffic Accounts Office, Railway Board

e: Station earnings pass from the station to the Cash Office of the railway, then into the accredited bank, and are finally adjusted through the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank at Nagpur, so option B gives the correct sequence.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the focal point system from Door Step Banking for the remittance of station earnings?

options.A: Under both systems, station staff carry cash personally to the Reserve Bank at Nagpur
options.B: The focal point system applies only to goods earnings, whereas Door Step Banking applies only to coaching earnings
options.C: Under the focal point system, stations remit their earnings to the nominated focal point branch of the accredited bank, whereas under Door Step Banking the bank collects the earnings from the railway premises itself
options.D: The focal point system has been replaced by the Traffic Book, whereas Door Step Banking has been replaced by E-Recon

e: Under the focal point system, stations remit earnings to the nominated focal point branch of the accredited bank. Under Door Step Banking the bank itself collects the earnings from the railway premises, so option C distinguishes them correctly.

q: The principal advantage claimed for E-Recon of transfer transactions between railways is that it:

options.A: Dispenses with the need for the respondent railway to accept a transaction
options.B: Converts all transfer transactions into cash transactions
options.C: Abolishes the head 'Transfer Railways' altogether
options.D: Enables transfer transactions raised by one railway to be matched and accepted by the respondent railway electronically and promptly, reducing the outstandings under 'Transfer Railways'

e: E-Recon enables transfer transactions raised by one railway to be matched and accepted by the respondent railway electronically and promptly. This reduces outstandings under Transfer Railways, though acceptance by the respondent is still required.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Subdivision I of the Development Fund (DF-I) is meant for works of passenger and other railway user amenities.
2. Subdivision III of the Development Fund (DF-III) is meant for unremunerative operational improvement works.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: DF-I of the Development Fund is meant for passenger and other railway user amenities, and DF-III is meant for unremunerative operational improvement works, with DF-II covering labour welfare, so both statements are correct.

q: During a year, a zonal railway collects rent for railway land given on licence, licence fees for the use of railway buildings and charges for advertisements displayed at stations. As these receipts are local and miscellaneous in nature and do not arise from traffic carried over more than one railway, they are taken to account as:

options.A: Other Coaching Earnings and apportioned among all railways
options.B: Goods earnings and apportioned in proportion to distance
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings accruing wholly to that railway
options.D: Receipts of the Public Account of India

e: Rent and licence fees for railway land and buildings and advertisement charges are local miscellaneous receipts not arising from traffic over more than one railway. They are Sundry Other Earnings accruing wholly to that railway, so option C is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'originating earnings' from 'apportioned earnings' of a zonal railway?

options.A: Originating earnings are the earnings initially collected and accounted for by the railway on which the traffic originates, whereas apportioned earnings are the share of the through-traffic earnings finally due to that railway after apportionment among all the railways concerned
options.B: Originating earnings relate only to goods traffic, whereas apportioned earnings relate only to coaching traffic
options.C: Both expressions denote the earnings held under Traffic Suspense
options.D: Originating earnings are credited to the Railway Board, whereas apportioned earnings are credited to the Reserve Bank

e: Originating earnings are the earnings initially collected and accounted for by the railway on which the traffic originates. Apportioned earnings are the share of through earnings finally due to that railway after apportionment, so option A is correct.

q: The expenditure on the ordinary working expenses of the Railways, provided for in the Demands for Grants, is an example of:

options.A: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Voted expenditure, voted by the Lok Sabha as part of the Demands for Grants
options.C: Expenditure from the Public Account requiring no appropriation
options.D: Expenditure met from the Contingency Fund of India

e: Ordinary working expenses provided in the Demands for Grants are voted expenditure, voted by the Lok Sabha as part of the Demands. They are not charged expenditure and are not met from the Public Account or Contingency Fund, so option B is correct.

q: A proposal is made to meet a shortfall under a revenue head of a zonal railway by re-appropriation from a capital head where savings are available. The correct position is that re-appropriation:

options.A: Is freely permissible between revenue and capital heads with the sanction of the General Manager
options.B: Is permissible between revenue and capital heads with the sanction of the Principal Financial Adviser
options.C: Is not permissible between the revenue and capital sections of a grant, nor between voted and charged expenditure
options.D: Is permissible only at the Final Modification Estimates stage in January

e: Re-appropriation is not permissible between the revenue and capital sections of a grant, nor between voted and charged expenditure, whatever the savings available. Such transfers need a fresh grant, so option C states the correct position.

q: A zonal railway finds, in November, that the grant for a service will be exhausted before the close of the year and that further funds will be needed during the same year. The requirement is correctly placed before Parliament during the year itself through:

options.A: An Excess Grant
options.B: A Vote of Credit
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts of the previous year
options.D: Supplementary Demands for Grants

e: When the grant for a service will be exhausted before the close of the year and more funds are needed in the same year, the requirement is placed before Parliament during the year through Supplementary Demands for Grants, so option D is correct.

q: A clerk is unable to incorporate a railway transaction directly in the Government accounts because the commercial accounts of the Railways are maintained in a different form from the Government accounts. The device by which the two sets of accounts are connected for this incorporation is the use of:

options.A: Link heads
options.B: Token grants
options.C: Budget proportions
options.D: Transfer certificates

e: Link heads connect the commercial accounts of the Railways, maintained in a different form, with the Government accounts. Through them a railway transaction is incorporated in the Government accounts, so option A is correct.

q: At the monthly review of outstandings, the Accounts Office of a zonal railway examines a report which lists the balances lying under the Provident Fund, deposits, suspense and remittance heads, so that old outstandings can be pursued. This report is the:

options.A: Pink Book
options.B: Debt Head Report
options.C: Traffic Book
options.D: Works Register

e: The report listing balances under the Provident Fund, deposits, suspense and remittance heads for review and pursuit of old outstandings is the Debt Head Report, rendered by the Accounts Office, so option B is correct.

q: The monthly Account Current rendered by a zonal railway is compiled from:

options.A: Only the station balance sheets received during the month
options.B: Only the Cash Book of the Cash and Pay Office
options.C: The Budget Estimates of the railway for the year
options.D: The General Books of the railway for the month, which embody the classified transactions of that month

e: The monthly Account Current is compiled from the General Books of the railway for the month, which embody the classified transactions of that month drawn from the subsidiary books and summaries, so option D is correct.

q: Along with the Revised Estimates for the current year framed in September, a zonal railway is required to frame, at the same stage, the:

options.A: Appropriation Accounts for the previous year
options.B: Final Modification Estimates for the current year
options.C: Excess Grants for the previous year
options.D: Budget Estimates for the ensuing year

e: At the September stage, along with the Revised Estimates for the current year, the zonal railway must also frame the Budget Estimates for the ensuing year, the two exercises being taken up together, so option D is correct.

q: The Provident Fund subscriptions recovered every month from the salaries of railway staff are held by the Government in trust for the staff and are accordingly accounted for in:

options.A: The Public Account of India, under the Provident Fund heads including Major Head 8009 for the State Railway Provident Fund
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India as revenue receipts of the Railways
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India
options.D: The Railway Pension Fund under the capital classification

e: Provident Fund subscriptions are held by Government in trust for staff and are accounted for in the Public Account of India, under the Provident Fund heads including Major Head 8009 for the State Railway Provident Fund, so option A is correct.

q: In the Accounts Office of a zonal railway, a bill received from an executive department is first entered in detail, transaction by transaction, before any classified summary is prepared from it. The books in which transactions are so recorded in detail in the first instance are the:

options.A: Subsidiary Books
options.B: General Books
options.C: Appropriation Accounts
options.D: Works Programme

e: Subsidiary Books are the books of first, detailed entry, in which bills and transactions are recorded transaction by transaction before any classified summary is prepared for the General Books, so option A is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ledger of a zonal railway is one of its General Books.
2. The Main Cash Book of a zonal railway is one of its Subsidiary Books.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Ledger is one of the General Books of a zonal railway, and the Main Cash Book is one of its Subsidiary Books in which cash transactions are first recorded in detail, so both statements are correct and option B applies.

q: The Principal Financial Adviser of a zonal railway has to render the monthly Account Current to the Railway Board. This Account Current is compiled from:

options.A: The station balance sheets received during the month only
options.B: The Main Cash Book of the Cash & Pay Office only
options.C: The General Books of the railway for the month
options.D: The Budget Register of the railway for the year

e: The monthly Account Current rendered by the Principal Financial Adviser to the Railway Board is compiled from the General Books of the railway for the month, not from station balance sheets or the Main Cash Book alone, so option C is correct.

q: At the close of a month, the Accounts Office of a zonal railway prepares a consolidated statement showing the outstanding balances under the Provident Fund, deposits, suspense and remittance heads, so that old outstandings under each head can be chased for clearance. This statement is the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Budget Register
options.C: Traffic Book
options.D: Debt Head Report

e: The consolidated statement of outstanding balances under the Provident Fund, deposits, suspense and remittance heads, prepared so old outstandings can be chased for clearance, is the Debt Head Report, so option D is correct.

q: A surprise check of the imprest held by an officer is carried out. The cash physically found with the holder, together with the paid vouchers held by him awaiting recoupment, should together equal:

options.A: The sanctioned amount of the imprest
options.B: The contingent expenditure of the previous month
options.C: The balance shown in the Main Cash Book
options.D: Half the annual contingent grant of his office

e: An imprest is a fixed advance: cash in hand plus paid vouchers awaiting recoupment must together equal the sanctioned imprest amount. Any difference shows a shortage or irregularity on surprise check, so option A is correct.

q: A debit balance under the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' in the books of a zonal railway represents:

options.A: Cheques issued by the railway which have not yet been paid by the bank
options.B: Amounts remitted by the Cash Office and the stations into the accredited bank, pending their adjustment against 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'
options.C: Provident Fund balances awaiting investment
options.D: Earnings still lying in cash at the stations

e: A debit balance under Remittances into Banks represents amounts remitted by the Cash Office and stations into the accredited bank that are still pending adjustment against Deposits with Reserve Bank, so option B is correct.

q: A cheque issued by a zonal railway in March is paid by the bank in April. The item is cleared from the suspense head 'Cheques and Bills' in the railway books:

options.A: On the date the cheque is issued by the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: On the date the payee receives the cheque
options.C: When the bank's intimation or advice of payment of the cheque is received
options.D: Automatically at the close of the financial year

e: A cheque is cleared from Cheques and Bills only when the bank's intimation or advice of payment is received, showing the cheque has actually been paid. Issue of the cheque alone does not clear the head, so option C is correct.

q: Balances outstanding under the suspense head 'Reserve Bank Suspense' in the books of a zonal railway are cleared:

options.A: By write-off under the sanction of the General Manager
options.B: Automatically at the end of five years
options.C: Only after the statutory audit of the year is completed
options.D: On receipt of the advice or intimation from the Reserve Bank of India

e: Balances under Reserve Bank Suspense are cleared on receipt of the advice or intimation from the Reserve Bank of India confirming the adjustment. They are not written off by the railway or cleared automatically, so option D is correct.

q: A transaction between a zonal railway and a State Government, routed through the Accountant General of the State, is pending clearance in the railway books. Pending clearance, the transaction is held under the suspense head:

options.A: AG Suspense
options.B: PAO Suspense
options.C: PSB Suspense
options.D: Traffic Suspense

e: A transaction with a State Government routed through the Accountant General of the State is held, pending clearance, under AG Suspense in the railway books. PAO and PSB Suspense cover other classes of transactions, so option A is correct.

q: A zonal railway has rendered services to an outside party and the amount due from that party is still to be realised. Pending realisation, the amount is debited to the suspense head:

options.A: Deposits
options.B: Demands Recoverable
options.C: Demands Payable
options.D: Cheques and Bills

e: Amounts due from an outside party for services rendered, pending realisation, are debited to Demands Recoverable, the head for dues recoverable by the Railways. On realisation the head is cleared, so option B is correct.

q: Goods and services have been received by a zonal railway from an outside supplier, but payment to the supplier is still to be made. Pending payment, the amount due is credited to the head:

options.A: Demands Recoverable
options.B: Miscellaneous Advances
options.C: Demands Payable
options.D: Reserve Bank Suspense

e: Amounts due to an outside supplier for goods and services received but not yet paid are credited to Demands Payable, the head for definite dues payable by the Railways, and cleared when payment is made, so option C is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'debt head' from a 'suspense head' in the railway accounts?

options.A: A debt head records transactions only temporarily, whereas a suspense head records definite liabilities
options.B: Both heads record only the cash balance held with the Reserve Bank
options.C: A debt head relates only to capital works, whereas a suspense head relates only to revenue works
options.D: A debt head records transactions representing definite liabilities of, or amounts recoverable by, the Government, whereas a suspense head records transactions only temporarily, pending adjustment to the final heads of account

e: A debt head records transactions representing definite liabilities of, or amounts recoverable by, Government. A suspense head records transactions only temporarily, pending adjustment to the final heads of account, so option D is correct.

q: An outside party deposits money with a zonal railway for a work to be executed by the railway on the party's behalf, and the deposit is credited to the 'Deposits' head. The expenditure incurred on that deposit work is:

options.A: Debited to the same 'Deposits' head, so that the work does not become a charge on railway revenues
options.B: Charged to the ordinary working expenses of the railway
options.C: Treated as a deduction from the earnings of the railway
options.D: Charged to Capital of the railway

e: Money deposited by an outside party for a work to be executed on its behalf is credited to Deposits, and the expenditure on that deposit work is debited to the same Deposits head, so the work is not a charge on railway revenues, so option A is correct.

q: A security deposit received from a contractor remains unclaimed for more than three years after it became due for refund. Such a deposit is:

options.A: Transferred to the Railway Pension Fund
options.B: Treated as a lapsed deposit and credited to the revenue of the Railways
options.C: Remitted to the Railway Board as its receipt
options.D: Retained permanently under the suspense heads

e: A contractor's security deposit that remains unclaimed for more than three years after it became due for refund is treated as a lapsed deposit and credited to the revenue of the Railways, so option B is correct.

q: During a year, a zonal railway needs to incur expenditure on a new service which was not contemplated in the approved Budget, but savings are available within the grant from which the expenditure can be met by re-appropriation. The approval of Parliament to the new service is obtained by presenting:

options.A: An Excess Grant after the close of the year
options.B: A Vote of Credit under Article 116
options.C: A token supplementary demand for a nominal amount
options.D: No demand at all, as re-appropriation by itself is sufficient

e: Where a new service not contemplated in the Budget can be financed by re-appropriation from savings within the grant, Parliament's approval to the new service is still obtained through a token supplementary demand for a nominal amount, so option C is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An Excess Grant is obtained during the financial year, before the excess expenditure is incurred.
2. Before a Demand for an Excess Grant is presented to the Lok Sabha, the excess expenditure is first examined by the Public Accounts Committee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 2 only

e: An Excess Grant under Article 115 is sought only after excess expenditure has actually been incurred, so statement 1 is false. The excess is first examined by the Public Accounts Committee before the Demand is presented, so statement 2 alone is correct.

q: Savings are available under a capital head of a zonal railway, and it is proposed to meet a shortfall under a revenue head by re-appropriation from the capital head. The correct position is that re-appropriation:

options.A: Is not permissible between the revenue and capital sections of a grant
options.B: Is permissible with the sanction of the Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: Is permissible with the concurrence of the Principal Financial Adviser alone
options.D: Is permissible only at the Final Modification Estimates stage

e: Re-appropriation is permitted only within the same section of a grant. Funds cannot be moved between the revenue and capital sections, as each section is a separate grant voted by Parliament, so such re-appropriation is not permissible.

q: In October, a zonal railway foresees that a part of the funds provided in its Budget for a service will remain unutilised during the year. The funds so foreseen to remain unutilised should be:

options.A: Retained till the last day of the financial year
options.B: Surrendered as soon as the savings are foreseen
options.C: Spent on any other work selected by the executive
options.D: Carried forward automatically to the next financial year

e: Under the Finance Code, savings foreseen during the year must be surrendered as soon as they are foreseen, and not retained till year-end. Timely surrender lets the Railway Board re-allot the funds usefully elsewhere in the same year.

q: Savings are available under one Primary Unit within a Sub-Major Head of Major Head 3002, and an excess is foreseen under another Primary Unit of the same Sub-Major Head. As the Sub-Major Head is the unit of appropriation for revenue expenditure, re-appropriation between the two Primary Units:

options.A: Requires a supplementary grant from Parliament in every case
options.B: Requires the sanction of the Railway Board in every case
options.C: Can be sanctioned at the zonal level by the competent authority, with finance concurrence
options.D: Is prohibited under the rules of re-appropriation

e: For revenue expenditure the Sub-Major Head is the unit of appropriation, not the Primary Unit. Re-appropriation between Primary Units within the same Sub-Major Head can therefore be sanctioned at zonal level by the competent authority with finance concurrence.

q: A dedicated fund was set up in 2001-02 to wipe out the arrears of replacement and renewal of over-aged safety-related assets such as track, bridges and signalling gear. That fund was the:

options.A: Railway Safety Fund
options.B: Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.C: Capital Fund
options.D: Special Railway Safety Fund

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund was set up in 2001-02 as a dedicated fund to wipe out arrears of renewal and replacement of over-aged safety assets like track, bridges and signalling gear. It is distinct from the later Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Safety Fund is credited with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares and also receives a share of the cess levied on petrol and diesel.
2. The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is financed through Gross Budgetary Support and the internal resources of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Railway Safety Fund receives the safety surcharge on passenger fares and a share of the cess on petrol and diesel. The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is financed from Gross Budgetary Support and Railways internal resources, so both statements are correct.

q: In a year in which the Railways earn no surplus, the annual appropriation from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is nevertheless:

options.A: Made only out of market borrowings raised through IRFC
options.B: Charged to the working expenses of the Railways, whether or not there is a surplus
options.C: Postponed indefinitely till a surplus arises
options.D: Met out of the balances of the Pension Fund

e: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is a charge on working expenses to provide for renewal and replacement of assets. It is made from revenue whether or not a surplus is earned, and is not postponed till a surplus arises.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriations to the Development Fund of the Railways are made out of the surplus of the Railways.
2. Appropriations to the Capital Fund of the Railways are made out of market borrowings raised through IRFC.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Appropriations to the Development Fund are made out of the surplus of the Railways after meeting working expenses and fund appropriations. Capital Fund appropriations are also from surplus, not from IRFC market borrowings, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A retiring railway servant covered under the old pension scheme is paid the commuted value of a portion of his pension. The commuted value so paid is debited to:

options.A: The ordinary working expenses under Sub-Major Head 11 of Major Head 3002
options.B: The Development Fund
options.C: The Capital Fund
options.D: The Railway Pension Fund

e: Commuted value of pension is a pensionary benefit of a servant under the old pension scheme. Such pensionary charges are met from the Railway Pension Fund, to which appropriations are made from revenue, so the payment is debited to that Fund.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Pension Fund meets the pensionary benefits of railway servants covered under the old defined-benefit pension scheme.
2. The retirement benefits of subscribers of the National Pension System are also paid out of the Railway Pension Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Railway Pension Fund meets pensionary benefits only of staff under the old defined-benefit scheme. National Pension System subscribers are governed by the separate NPS architecture and their benefits are not paid from this Fund, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: In the accounts of a zonal railway, the allocation of a work is written as 'RRSK-3300'. This allocation indicates:

options.A: A work of track renewal (Plan Head 31) financed from the Railway Safety Fund
options.B: A work of signalling and telecommunication (Plan Head 33) financed from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.C: A work of staff quarters (Plan Head 51) financed from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.D: A work of bridge renewal (Plan Head 32) financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: In the allocation, the prefix shows the source of finance and the number shows the Plan Head. RRSK denotes Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh and 33 is Signalling and Telecommunication works, so RRSK-3300 is an S and T work financed from RRSK.

q: In the accounts of a zonal railway, the allocation of a work is written as 'DRF-3200'. This allocation indicates:

options.A: A work of track renewal (Plan Head 31) financed from Capital
options.B: Rolling Stock (Plan Head 21) financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: A bridge work, including tunnel works and approaches (Plan Head 32), financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: A work of passenger amenities (Plan Head 53) financed from the Development Fund

e: DRF denotes the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Plan Head 32 covers Bridge Works including tunnels and approaches. Hence DRF-3200 is a bridge work financed from DRF, the normal source for renewal of bridges on age and condition.

q: A clerk proposes to classify the works expenditure of a zonal railway through Sub-Major Heads and its revenue working expenses through Plan Heads. The correct position is that:

options.A: Both works and revenue expenditure are classified through Plan Heads
options.B: Both works and revenue expenditure are classified through Sub-Major Heads
options.C: Works expenditure is classified under Major Head 3002 and revenue expenditure under Major Head 5002
options.D: Capital (works) expenditure is classified under Major Head 5002 by Plan Heads, while revenue expenditure is classified under Major Head 3002 by Sub-Major Heads

e: Capital or works expenditure is classified under Major Head 5002 by Plan Heads, which show the purpose of investment. Revenue working expenses are classified under Major Head 3002 by Sub-Major Heads, the erstwhile Demands 3 to 14, so the clerk proposal is reversed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The erstwhile Demand No. 1 (Railway Board) and Demand No. 2 (Miscellaneous Expenditure) of the separate Railway Budget are now accounted for under Major Head 3001.
2. The erstwhile Demand No. 16 (capital expenditure) of the separate Railway Budget is now accounted for under Major Head 3002.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Erstwhile Demands 1 and 2, Railway Board and Miscellaneous Expenditure, are now under Major Head 3001, so statement 1 is correct. Erstwhile Demand 16, capital expenditure, is under Major Head 5002 and not 3002, so statement 2 is false.

q: The expenditure of the Railway Board and of central organisations of the Railways, such as the Research Designs and Standards Organisation, is classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Major Head 3002
options.B: Major Head 5002
options.C: Major Head 3001
options.D: Major Head 1001

e: Major Head 3001 covers Indian Railways - Policy Formulation, Direction, Research and Other Central Organisations. Expenditure of the Railway Board and central organisations like RDSO is therefore classified under Major Head 3001.

q: The Traffic Book of a zonal railway, in which the results of apportionment of earnings are adjusted, is compiled in:

options.A: The Cash & Pay Office of the zonal railway
options.B: The Railway Board's office, directly from the returns rendered by stations
options.C: The Divisional Accounts Office of the division concerned
options.D: The Traffic Accounts Office, from the station balance sheets and the apportionment statements

e: The Traffic Book, which adjusts the results of apportionment of earnings between railways, is compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office. It is built up from station balance sheets and the apportionment statements received for coaching and goods traffic.

q: Cash collected at a station is sent by the station to the Cash Office and the bank for remittance. The cash so sent is accompanied by the document known as the:

options.A: Cash Remittance Note
options.B: Transfer Certificate
options.C: Advice of Internal Check
options.D: Error Sheet

e: Cash collected at stations is remitted to the Cash Office and bank accompanied by a Cash Remittance Note. The note advises the Cash Office of the amount and mode of remittance and supports the credit taken in the station balance sheet.

q: For the information of the Railway Board and the management, the approximate gross earnings of a zonal railway are compiled and reported at intervals of:

options.A: Every day
options.B: Every ten days
options.C: Every two months
options.D: Every quarter

e: Approximate gross earnings are compiled and reported to the Railway Board and management every ten days. This ten-day periodical return gives a quick picture of earnings trends during the month for budgetary and operational control.

q: The proposals and estimates contained in the Budget of the Railways are explained, for the information of Parliament, in the Budget document known as the:

options.A: Pink Book
options.B: Outcome Budget
options.C: Explanatory Memorandum
options.D: Appropriation Accounts

e: The Explanatory Memorandum is the Budget document that explains the proposals and estimates in the Demands for Grants for the information of Parliament. The Pink Book, by contrast, lists works and is an internal budget document of the Railways.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways is divided into two sections, namely:

options.A: Plan and Non-Plan
options.B: Voted and Charged
options.C: Railway Board and Zonal Railways
options.D: Revenue and Capital

e: After merger with the Union Budget, the Railways have a single Demand for Grants. That Demand is divided into a Revenue section, covering Major Heads 3001 and 3002, and a Capital section, covering Major Head 5002, so the division is Revenue and Capital.

q: The General Manager of a zonal railway asks why the budget allotment for the year has not been communicated before the Budget is presented to Parliament. Ordinarily, the budget allotment for a financial year is communicated by the Railway Board to the zonal railways:

options.A: After the Appropriation Act for the year has been passed
options.B: Before the presentation of the Budget in Parliament
options.C: Along with the Revised Estimates in September
options.D: Only at the Final Modification Estimates stage in January

e: Budget allotments can be communicated only after Parliament has voted the Demands and the Appropriation Act has been passed, since no expenditure can be authorised before appropriation by law. The Board therefore communicates allotments after the Act is passed.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the budget estimates received from the zonal railways are consolidated and submitted to the Ministry of Finance for inclusion in the Union Budget by:

options.A: The Controller General of Accounts
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: Each zonal railway separately
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: After the Budget merger, zonal railways submit their estimates to the Railway Board. The Board consolidates them and submits the single Railway Demand to the Ministry of Finance for inclusion in the Union Budget, so consolidation rests with the Railway Board.

q: During the voting on a Demand for Grant of the Ministry of Railways, a member of the Lok Sabha moves an amendment to increase the amount of the Demand. In voting on a Demand for Grant, the Lok Sabha:

options.A: Can increase the amount with the permission of the Speaker
options.B: Can increase the amount if the Finance Minister agrees
options.C: Can assent to the Demand, refuse it or reduce the amount demanded, but cannot increase the amount of the Demand
options.D: Can increase only the charged portion of the Demand

e: Under Article 113, the Lok Sabha may assent to a Demand, refuse it, or reduce the amount demanded. It has no power to increase a Demand, as the Demand represents the maximum expenditure proposed by the Government, so option C states the position correctly.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha can vote on the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways.
2. Cut motions on Demands for Grants can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 2 only

e: Voting on Demands for Grants is the exclusive power of the Lok Sabha under Article 113; the Rajya Sabha can only discuss them. Cut motions, being part of voting on Demands, can likewise be moved only in the Lok Sabha, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: While examining the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways, a clerk notices that certain figures of expenditure are printed in italics. In the Demands for Grants, figures printed in italics represent:

options.A: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Supplementary estimates for the year
options.C: Capital expenditure of the Railways
options.D: Amounts surrendered during the previous year

e: In the Demands for Grants, charged expenditure is distinguished by being printed in italics. Charged expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 112(3) and is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it is discussed.

q: The arithmetical accuracy of the monthly accounts compiled in the General Books of a zonal railway is proved by preparing a:

options.A: Classified Abstract
options.B: Trial Balance
options.C: Suspense Register
options.D: Debt Head Report

e: The arithmetical accuracy of the monthly accounts in the General Books is proved by a Trial Balance. Agreement of total debits and credits in the Trial Balance shows that postings from the Classified Abstract to the Ledger have been correctly made.

q: The annual Balance Sheet of a zonal railway, showing its assets and liabilities, is prepared from:

options.A: The Pink Book of the railway
options.B: The Budget Register of the railway
options.C: The balances appearing in the General Books (Ledger) of the railway
options.D: The Traffic Book of the railway

e: The annual Balance Sheet of a zonal railway is prepared from the balances standing in its General Books, that is the Ledger. Those balances show the assets, liabilities, capital-at-charge and fund balances of the railway at the close of the year.

q: Which of the following units of the Railways is an independent accounting unit which renders its own monthly Account Current to the Railway Board?

options.A: A railway division of a zonal railway
options.B: A large railway station
options.C: A sub-divisional engineering office
options.D: A production unit, such as the Integral Coach Factory

e: A production unit like the Integral Coach Factory is an independent accounting unit. It compiles its own accounts and renders its own monthly Account Current to the Railway Board, unlike a division, whose accounts merge in the zonal railway accounts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Accounts of the Railways from their Appropriation Accounts?

options.A: The Finance Accounts present the receipts and disbursements of the year classified under the Major Heads of account, whereas the Appropriation Accounts compare the expenditure of the year with the grants voted by Parliament
options.B: The Finance Accounts compare the expenditure of the year with the grants, whereas the Appropriation Accounts present the receipts under the Major Heads
options.C: The Finance Accounts are prepared only for the transactions of the Railway Board's office
options.D: The Finance Accounts contain the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Finance Accounts present the actual receipts and disbursements of the year classified under the Major Heads of account. Appropriation Accounts compare actual expenditure with the grants voted by Parliament and explain variations, so option A distinguishes them correctly.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Vote on Account is a grant in advance, voted by the Lok Sabha to meet expenditure for a part of the financial year pending the passing of the full Budget.
2. An Interim Budget presents the estimates of receipts and expenditure for the whole financial year, though major policy changes are generally avoided in it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A Vote on Account under Article 116 is a grant in advance for part of the year pending passing of the full Budget, so statement 1 is correct. An Interim Budget covers estimates for the whole year, though major policy changes are generally avoided, so both are correct.

q: During the discussion on a Demand for Grant in the Lok Sabha, a member moves a cut motion proposing that the amount of the Demand be reduced by a specified amount to bring out a particular grievance relating to economy in expenditure. Such a motion is known as an:

options.A: Economy cut motion
options.B: Policy cut motion
options.C: Token cut motion
options.D: Guillotine motion

e: An Economy Cut motion seeks reduction of a Demand by a specified amount to raise a grievance about economy in expenditure on a service. It differs from a Policy Cut, which reduces the Demand to Re 1, and a Token Cut, which reduces it by Rs 100.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Interest payments and debt charges of the Government of India are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
2. Charged expenditure is nevertheless included in the Appropriation Act passed by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Interest payments and debt charges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 112(3) and are not voted by Parliament, so statement 1 is correct. Charged expenditure is still included in the Appropriation Act under Article 114, so both statements are correct.

q: The duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in relation to the audit of the accounts of the Union and the States are prescribed by Parliament by law under the Constitution in:

options.A: Article 148
options.B: Article 149
options.C: Article 150
options.D: Article 151

e: Article 149 of the Constitution provides that the Comptroller and Auditor General shall perform such duties and exercise such powers in relation to audit of Union and State accounts as are prescribed by Parliament by law. Article 148 only creates the office.

q: A clerk proposes to exhibit the transactions of the Contingency Fund of India under Major Head 8658 along with the suspense heads. In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Contingency Fund is classified under Major Head:
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Contingency Fund of India is recorded under Major Head 8000 in Part II of the Government accounts. Major Head 8658 is Suspense Accounts and cannot be used for Contingency Fund transactions.

q: A zonal railway holds its cash balance with the Reserve Bank of India, but a clerk proposes to exhibit 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' under Major Head 8658. In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' is correctly classified under Major Head:
e: Deposits with Reserve Bank is Major Head 8675 in the List of Major and Minor Heads, under the Suspense and Miscellaneous section of the Public Account. It shows the cash balance of the Government held with the Reserve Bank of India.

q: In the accounts of a zonal railway, the allocation of a work is written as 'RSF-2900'. This allocation indicates that the work is:

options.A: Financed from the Railway Safety Fund and classified under Plan Head 29 for road safety works relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges
options.B: Financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund and classified under Plan Head 29 for road safety works relating to level crossings
options.C: Financed from the Railway Safety Fund and classified under Plan Head 29 for road safety works relating to level crossings
options.D: Financed from Capital and classified under Plan Head 29

e: RSF denotes the Railway Safety Fund and Plan Head 29 covers Road Safety Works - Level Crossings. Hence RSF-2900 is a level crossing safety work financed from the Railway Safety Fund; road over and under bridges fall under Plan Head 30.

q: A zonal railway takes up a work of providing additional passenger amenities at a station and finances it from the Development Fund. In its accounts, the allocation of the work is correctly written as:
e: Plan Head 53 covers Passenger Amenities, and works for additional passenger amenities financed from the Development Fund take the source prefix DF. The correct allocation is therefore DF-5300, source first and Plan Head number following it.

q: An asset of a zonal railway, whose original cost stands in the Block Account, is sold and removed from the assets of the railway. On such sale and removal, the Block Account of the railway is:

options.A: Increased by the sale value realised for the asset
options.B: Left unchanged, as the Block Account is never altered after creation of the asset
options.C: Reduced by the sale value realised for the asset
options.D: Reduced by the original cost of the asset so sold and removed

e: The Block Account records assets at their original cost. When an asset is sold and removed, the Block Account is reduced by the original cost of that asset, not by the sale value realised, which is separately credited as per the source of finance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of renewal or replacement of an asset, when met from the Depreciation Reserve Fund, is not added to the Capital-at-charge of the Railways.
2. The original cost of an asset so renewed continues to be exhibited in the Block Account of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Renewal or replacement met from the Depreciation Reserve Fund is not added to Capital-at-charge, since no fresh capital is invested, so statement 1 is correct. The original cost of the renewed asset continues in the Block Account, so statement 2 is also correct.

q: A railway servant who retires under the old pension scheme is paid death-cum-retirement gratuity on retirement. In the railway accounts, this gratuity, being a pensionary charge, is met by debit to the:

options.A: Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Development Fund
options.C: Pension Fund
options.D: Capital Fund

e: Death-cum-retirement gratuity is a pensionary charge of a servant under the old pension scheme. Pensionary charges are met from the Railway Pension Fund, built up by appropriations from revenue, so the gratuity is debited to the Pension Fund.

q: A bridge on a zonal railway, which has become due for renewal on age and condition, is renewed and the cost is financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund. Notwithstanding the source of finance, the work continues to be classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 32 for Bridge Works
options.B: Plan Head 31 for Track Renewals
options.C: Plan Head 30 for road safety works
options.D: Plan Head 42 for Workshops

e: Classification by Plan Head follows the nature of the work, not the source of finance. A bridge renewal, even when financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund, remains a Bridge Work and is classified under Plan Head 32.

q: At the close of a month, the Accounts Office of a zonal railway prepares a head-wise summary of the transactions recorded in its subsidiary books, from which the postings are made to the General Books. A clerk calls this summary the Debt Head Report. The summary is correctly known as the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Classified Abstract
options.C: Account Current
options.D: Suspense Register

e: The Classified Abstract is the monthly head-wise summary of transactions recorded in the subsidiary books. Postings to the General Books are made from it, and it must not be confused with the Debt Head Report, which shows debt and suspense balances.

q: A cash payment made through the Cash and Pay Office of a zonal railway is entered by a clerk in the Journal Book. Cash receipts and payments are correctly recorded, in the first instance, in the:

options.A: Ledger
options.B: Classified Abstract
options.C: Journal Book itself, as all entries originate there
options.D: Main Cash Book

e: Cash receipts and payments are recorded in the first instance in the Main Cash Book maintained by the Cash and Pay Office. The Journal Book is for transfer and adjustment entries, and entries reach the Ledger through the Classified Abstract.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balances outstanding under the suspense heads of a railway are reviewed periodically so that the items held under them are cleared by adjustment to the final heads of account as early as possible.
2. An item once booked under a suspense head may properly be left there indefinitely, as suspense heads are meant for permanent retention of unadjusted items.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Suspense heads are only temporary resting places for items awaiting final adjustment, so balances under them must be reviewed periodically and cleared early, making statement 1 correct. Leaving items indefinitely, as in statement 2, defeats their purpose and is wrong.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation raises funds from the market on behalf of the Railways and acquires rolling stock which is leased to the Railways. The debt so raised is serviced by:

options.A: The Ministry of Finance directly, without any charge on the Railways
options.B: The Railways, through lease charges paid to the Corporation
options.C: The State Governments over whose territory the rolling stock runs
options.D: The Depreciation Reserve Fund, without any payment by the Railways

e: IRFC raises market funds and leases rolling stock to the Railways. The Railways service this debt by paying lease charges to IRFC, comprising capital recovery and interest, so the borrowing is ultimately serviced by the Railways and not by the Finance Ministry.

q: Certain lines of the Railways are maintained for strategic considerations and their working results in a loss. The working losses of such Strategic Lines are borne through a subsidy provided by:

options.A: General Revenues
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: The Railway Safety Fund
options.D: The Capital Fund

e: Strategic lines are maintained for strategic considerations though they run at a loss. Their working losses are borne by General Revenues through a subsidy, since the lines are not commercially viable and are kept open at the instance of the Government.

q: Parliament is called upon to make a grant for a special purpose which does not form part of the current service of any financial year. A grant of this nature, made under Article 116 of the Constitution, is known as an:

options.A: Excess Grant
options.B: Supplementary Grant
options.C: Exceptional Grant
options.D: Token Grant

e: An Exceptional Grant under Article 116 is a grant for a special purpose which forms no part of the current service of any financial year. It differs from a Supplementary Grant for an existing service and from an Excess Grant for excess already incurred.

q: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted, under Article 151 of the Constitution, to the:

options.A: Finance Minister
options.B: President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament
options.C: Speaker of the Lok Sabha directly
options.D: Public Accounts Committee directly

e: Under Article 151, the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to the Union accounts are submitted to the President. The President causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament, after which the Public Accounts Committee examines them.

q: After the Demands for Grants have been voted by the Lok Sabha, the Appropriation Bill is introduced to authorise withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India. In respect of this Bill, the Constitution provides that:

options.A: Any amendment varying the amount of a grant may be moved in either House
options.B: The Rajya Sabha may amend the Bill so as to alter the destination of a grant
options.C: The Bill may be introduced in either House of Parliament
options.D: No amendment shall be proposed which will have the effect of varying the amount, or altering the destination, of any grant so made, or of varying the amount of any expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund

e: Article 114(2) bars any amendment to the Appropriation Bill that varies the amount or alters the destination of a grant already voted, or varies charged expenditure. The Bill only authorises withdrawal of the amounts already sanctioned by the Lok Sabha.

q: A doubt arises whether a Bill introduced in Parliament is a Money Bill within the meaning of the Constitution. The decision on this question rests finally with the:

options.A: President
options.B: Speaker of the Lok Sabha, whose decision is final
options.C: Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Finance Minister

e: Under Article 110(3), if a question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is final. The Speaker also endorses the Money Bill certificate when it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha and the President.
